Lists & Navigation

HTML Living Standard

Turn items into lists and connect pages using readable links, file paths, and fragment identifiers.

Open interactive lesson

On this page

  • Choose among three list types

Choose among three list types

Use ul when order is incidental, ol when sequence or ranking matters, and dl for terms with descriptions. A nested list belongs inside the li it expands. Set start on ol to continue numbering or type to choose a numbering style.

How to try it In index.html, replace the content between <body> and </body> with this example. Save the file and reload it in the browser.

<ul>
  <li>Supplies<ul><li>Notebook</li><li>Pencil</li></ul></li>
</ul>
<ol start="3" type="1"><li>Open your file</li><li>Check the page</li></ol>
<dl><dt>DOM</dt><dd>The page represented as a tree.</dd></dl>

What to expect The numbered steps start at 3. The supplies have a nested list.

Write links that name their destination

The href holds the destination. The text inside a should help people predict what opens. For an intentional new tab, use target="_blank" and rel="noopener" and say that a new tab opens.

How to try it In index.html, replace the content between <body> and </body> with this example. Save the file and reload it in the browser.

<a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/"
   target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read the HTML reference (new tab)</a>

What to expect The label identifies the destination before you select it.

Relative and absolute file paths

Relative paths start from the current document’s folder. From work/project.html, ./notes.html stays inside work and ../index.html goes up one folder. A leading slash starts from the website root. An absolute URL includes the scheme and host and can point to another site. Save the matching files first, then test each link.

<a href="./notes.html">Project notes</a>
<a href="../index.html">Home</a>
<a href="https://example.com/">Partner website</a>

Jump to a section or start an action

Use # plus an id to target a section on the same page. mailto: and tel: hand off to a configured email or phone app. The download attribute requests downloading a linked file and works with same-origin URLs and blob or data URLs.

How to try it In index.html, replace the content between <body> and </body> with this example. Save the file and reload it in the browser.

<p><a href="#contact">Jump to contact</a></p>
<h2 id="contact">Contact</h2>
<a href="mailto:hello@example.com">Email us</a>
<a href="tel:+12025550140">Call the office</a>
<a href="data:text/plain,Workshop%20checklist" download="checklist.txt">Download checklist</a>

What to expect The first link targets the Contact heading.

Hands-on exercise

Make index.html, projects.html, and contact.html. Give each page links to the other two. Move projects.html into a work folder and update the links both ways.
